grupos.bajada: Risk cut-offs, nuchal translucency, secondary markers and management.
grupos.html:
1Risk cut-offs of combined screening

The Calculator lets you choose the cut-off. By default it uses Fetal Medicine Barcelona; Nicolaides 2005 (FMF) is available as an alternative.

RiskFetal Medicine BarcelonaNicolaides 2005 (FMF)
Very high≥1/10—
High1/11 – 1/250≥1/100
Intermediate1/251 – 1/11001/101 – 1/1000
Low<1/1100<1/1000

Own table CaVeSal® · Based on: Fetal Medicine Barcelona · Nicolaides KH 2005 (FMF)

2Management by risk — Fetal Medicine Barcelona cut-off

  • Very high (≥1/10): genetic counselling and offer invasive testing with microarray. If the woman prefers, NIPT may be accepted, unless there is an ultrasound anomaly or increased NT.
  • High (1/11–1/250): genetic counselling; NIPT or invasive testing according to informed choice (NIPT carries no miscarriage risk, detects ~99 % of T21, only the chromosomes studied; invasive testing carries a 0.1–0.2 % loss risk and studies all chromosomes). With an ultrasound anomaly or NT >p99: chorionic villus sampling + microarray.
  • Intermediate (1/251–1/1100): report the result and offer NIPT to complete screening. If NIPT is positive, confirm with invasive testing.
  • Low (<1/1100): give the result and explain the limitations of screening.

Own algorithm CaVeSal® · Based on: Fetal Medicine Barcelona — aneuploidy screening protocol

3Management by risk — Nicolaides 2005 (FMF) cut-off

  • High (≥1/100): offer invasive testing (CVS <14 wk / amniocentesis ≥15 wk) and genetic counselling. NIPT can now be offered as a non-invasive alternative.
  • Intermediate (1/101–1/1000): second-stage first-trimester ultrasound (nasal bone, tricuspid regurgitation or ductus venosus Doppler); offer CVS if the adjusted risk reaches 1/100 or more. NIPT is now an alternative.
  • Low (<1/1000): no further testing.

Own algorithm CaVeSal® · Based on: Nicolaides KH. Am J Obstet Gynecol 2005 (FMF)

4Nuchal translucency (NT)

  • NT is compared with the median and 95th percentile expected for the CRL.
  • NT ≥3.5 mm: high risk regardless of age. Increased chromosomal and cardiac risk: refer to Fetal Medicine, CVS or amniocentesis, fetal echocardiography.
  • NT ≥p95 for CRL: increased chromosomal risk; offer NIPT or invasive diagnosis and fetal echocardiography. With maternal age ≥35 years, the risk is considered high.
  • Normal NT with age ≥35 years: age is an a priori risk factor; consider combined screening or NIPT according to the woman's preference.

Based on: Snijders RJ et al. 1998 · Nicolaides KH 2005 (FMF)

5First-trimester secondary markers

FindingInterpretation and management
Absent nasal boneLR+ ~6 for T21. Integrate with NT and other markers.
Ductus venosus with absent or reversed a-waveMarker of aneuploidy and congenital heart disease. Refer to Fetal Medicine, echocardiography.
Tricuspid regurgitationAssociated with T21 and congenital heart disease. Fetal echocardiography.
Choroid plexus cyst(s)Soft marker, more associated with T18 than T21. Isolated with normal screening: low residual risk.
2 or more abnormal markersHigh chromosomal risk: offer invasive diagnosis (CVS 11–13+6 wk).

Own table CaVeSal® · Based on: Cicero S et al. (nasal bone) · Kagan KO et al. (TR and DV) · FMF/Nicolaides

6First-trimester megacystis

  • 7–14.9 mm: aneuploidy risk ~20–25 % (T13/T18 more than T21): offer karyotype or NIPT. Ultrasound follow-up every 2–4 weeks; spontaneous resolution is common if isolated and euploid.
  • ≥15 mm: low aneuploidy risk if isolated, but ~90 % progressive obstructive uropathy (posterior urethral valves, more frequent in male fetuses). Refer to Fetal Medicine / fetal urology.

Based on: FMF/Nicolaides — first-trimester megacystis

7NIPT result

  • Positive NIPT: confirm with invasive diagnosis (amniocentesis or CVS), genetic counselling and referral to Fetal Medicine.
  • Negative NIPT: low but not zero residual risk; routine ultrasound follow-up.

Based on: Fetal Medicine Barcelona · FMF

Full sources for this tab: Calculator bibliography.

grupos.bajada: Uterine artery Doppler, ophthalmic artery, biomarkers, MAP and aspirin.
grupos.html:
1First-trimester markers and their thresholds

MarkerHighModerate
Mean uterine artery PI (1st trim.)≥2.35 (>p95)1.90–2.34 (p90–95)
PAPP-A (MoM)<0.30.3–0.39
PlGF (MoM)<0.50.5–0.69
Free β-hCG (MoM)>3.02.5–3.0
MAP in the 1st trimester—>90 mmHg

Own table CaVeSal® · Based on: FMF/Nicolaides · Fetal Medicine Barcelona · Poon LC et al. FIGO 2019

2How first-trimester markers are combined

  • 2 or more high markers: high risk of early PE. Prescribe aspirin, serial PlGF and refer to Fetal Medicine.
  • 1 high + 1 moderate: moderate-high risk. Prescribe aspirin and reassess with 2nd-trimester uterine artery PI and sFlt-1/PlGF.
  • 1 high marker: aspirin according to the FMF combined risk; uterine artery PI check in the 2nd trimester.
  • 2 or more moderate: close surveillance, consider aspirin, reassess in the 2nd trimester.
  • 1 moderate: routine follow-up, integrating other clinical factors.
  • All normal: baseline risk.

Own algorithm CaVeSal® · Based on: FMF · Fetal Medicine Barcelona · FIGO 2019

3Aspirin to prevent preeclampsia

Aspirin ~150 mg every night from 11–14+6 wk until 36 wk, delivery or diagnosis of PE (FIGO 2019, regimen preferred by CaVeSal®). Alternative: 81 mg/day from 12–28 wk (ideally before 16) until delivery (ACOG PB 222, 2020).

Indications in the Calculator: high risk in first-trimester screening (uterine artery PI, PlGF, ophthalmic artery or combination of markers) and pre-pregnancy obesity.

Based on: Poon LC et al. FIGO 2019 · ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222 (2020)

4Ophthalmic artery — PSV2/PSV1 ratio

RatioInterpretation
<0.70Normal. In established PE it suggests less systemic vascular involvement.
0.70–0.77Borderline / grey zone. Monitor with uterine artery PI and PlGF; in the 2nd/3rd trimester repeat in 48–72 h and assess sFlt-1/PlGF.
≥0.78High risk of PE and FGR (independent predictor). In the 1st trimester: aspirin. In established PE: severe vascular involvement, refer to Fetal Medicine.

Own algorithm CaVeSal® · Based on: Gyselaers W et al. UOG 2020 · Verlohren S et al. AJOG 2012 · Kaituʻu-Lino TJ et al. UOG 2018 · Fetal Medicine Barcelona

5Uterine artery PI in the 2nd trimester

  • ≥1.80 (high): fetal growth surveillance and follow-up Doppler at 28–32 wk.
  • 1.44–1.79 (moderate): serial biometry and Doppler in the 3rd trimester.

Based on: FMF · Fetal Medicine Barcelona

6sFlt-1/PlGF ratio

RatioManagement
≤38Rules out PE within the next week (NPV >99 %). Routine follow-up.
38 – 85 (<34 wk) · 38 – 110 (≥34 wk)Grey zone: repeat in 1–2 weeks, daily BP and proteinuria.
>85 (<34 wk) · >110 (≥34 wk)High suspicion of PE: proteinuria, liver and renal function; admit if there is maternal or fetal compromise.
>655Imminent PE: urgent admission; individualised delivery according to GA and maternal-fetal condition.

Fetal lung maturation and magnesium sulfate: see the cards Fetal lung maturation and Magnesium sulfate.

Based on: Roche/BRAHMS (sFlt-1/PlGF) · ISSHP · FMF

7Mean arterial pressure (MAP)

  • MAP = (SBP + 2 × DBP) / 3.
  • MAP >90 mmHg in the 1st trimester: higher risk of PE; consider aspirin according to the combined risk.
  • MAP ≥105 mmHg: warning sign of gestational hypertension or PE, especially after 20 wk; assess proteinuria, sFlt-1/PlGF and liver and renal function.

Based on: FMF · WHO · NICE · ISUOG

See also in Clinical History: MAP as a predictor · Hypertensive disorders — classification · Aspirin prophylaxis and antihypertensive management

grupos.bajada: CRL, 2nd- and 3rd-trimester biometry, humerus, cerebellum and estimated fetal weight.
grupos.html:
1GA by CRL (1st trimester)

  • Robinson and Fleming formula (1975), the FMF standard, for CRL from 10 to 84 mm.
  • With GA by CRL the Calculator corrects the LMP and recalculates the EDD (corrected LMP + 280 days).
  • In the 1st trimester GA by CRL is the most accurate; if it differs from the LMP, ultrasound takes priority.

Based on: Robinson HP, Fleming JE. Br J Obstet Gynaecol 1975

2GA by 2nd- and 3rd-trimester biometry

  • Estimates GA with BPD, HC, AC and FL (Hadlock 1984) and compares the parameters with each other.
  • Difference ≤7 days: concordant biometry, symmetric growth.
  • 8–14 days: moderate discordance; monitor progression.
  • >14 days: significant discordance; assess asymmetry. If AC is the lagging parameter, consider asymmetric FGR (see the Growth tab).

Own algorithm CaVeSal® · Based on: Hadlock FP et al. 1984

3Humerus length and humerus/femur ratio

  • GA by humerus follows Chitty and Altman (2002). Normal H/FL ratio: 0.87–1.01.
  • <0.85: rhizomelic shortening; suspected skeletal dysplasia (achondroplasia, hypochondroplasia). Refer to Fetal Medicine.
  • >1.05: relatively short femur; assess in clinical context.

Based on: Chitty LS, Altman DG 2002

4Transverse cerebellar diameter (TCD)

  • Between 14 and 28 wk the TCD in mm roughly equals GA in weeks; afterwards it is estimated from tables.
  • The cerebellum is spared in haemodynamic redistribution: a preserved TCD in a fetus with FGR confirms that the assigned GA is correct.
  • Small TCD for GA: suspected cerebellar hypoplasia; refer to Fetal Medicine and rule out Dandy-Walker and other CNS malformations.
  • At the lower limit: repeat in 3–4 weeks.

Own algorithm CaVeSal® · Based on: Goldstein I et al. 1987

5Estimated fetal weight (EFW)

  • Hadlock 4-parameter formula (BPD, HC, AC, FL).
  • Percentile by Figueras 2008 (Fetal Medicine Barcelona, adjusted for fetal sex) or by INTERGROWTH-21st, as chosen.
EFWCategory by absolute weight
<1,000 gExtremely low weight
1,000–1,499 gVery low weight
<2,500 gLow weight (WHO)
2,500–3,999 gNormal weight
≥4,000 gMacrosomia
≥4,500 gSevere macrosomia

Based on: Hadlock FP et al. 1984 · Figueras F et al. EJOGRB 2008 · INTERGROWTH-21st

See also in Clinical History: Pregnancy duration and EDD · Ultrasound by trimester

grupos.bajada: EFW percentile, macrosomia, FL/AC ratio and head circumference.
grupos.html:
1Classification by EFW percentile

PercentileClassificationManagement
<P3FGR (sole criterion)Refer to Fetal Medicine; urgent full Doppler (UA, MCA, CPR, DV); biometry every 1–2 wk.
P3–P10 with abnormal DopplerFGRClassify stage I–IV; follow-up every 1–2 wk; delivery according to GA and Doppler.
P3–P10 with normal DopplerSGA (healthy small)Biometry every 2–3 wk; delivery ≥40 wk if progress is favourable.
P10–P90AGARoutine follow-up.
P90–P96Borderline LGAMonitor; biometry at 38 wk.
≥P97Significant LGAReal risk of complications; check at 38–39 wk.

Own table CaVeSal® · Based on: Figueras F et al. 2008 · Fetal Medicine Barcelona protocol (Nov 2024) · ISUOG Delphi 2020

2Macrosomia by estimated weight

  • EFW ≥4,500 g: severe macrosomia; planned caesarean recommended (ACOG/NICE). Shoulder dystocia risk 14–22 %.
  • EFW ≥4,000 g: close surveillance; shoulder dystocia risk 3–4 %. In diabetic women consider caesarean. Ultrasound check at 38–39 wk.
  • EFW 3,800–3,999 g: upper limit; serial biometry, especially in diabetic women.

Based on: ACOG · NICE · Fetal Medicine Barcelona protocol — macrosomia (Sep 2024)

3FL/AC ratio (asymmetry)

FL/AC ratioInterpretation
0.16–0.235Normal: symmetric growth.
>0.235Disproportionately small AC: suspected late asymmetric FGR. Umbilical and MCA Doppler, biometry every 2 wk; refer if Doppler is abnormal.
<0.16Disproportionately short femur: assess humerus; soft aneuploidy marker if isolated; refer if skeletal dysplasia is suspected.

Own algorithm CaVeSal® · Based on: Hadlock FP et al. · fetal biometry literature

4Head circumference and GA in asymmetry

  • HC <p3 for GA: microcephaly; refer to Fetal Medicine, neurosonography, rule out congenital infection (TORCH), chromosomal abnormality or genetic cause.
  • HC close to p3: check in 3–4 wk; neurosonography if it persists.
  • In asymmetric FGR or with uncertain LMP in the 3rd trimester, HC and FL are the most reliable parameters to estimate GA. In the 3rd trimester the LMP is not corrected: it is used as an approximate reference.

Based on: Chitty LS et al. 1994 · Jeanty P 1983

See also in Clinical History: Fetal growth SGA/FGR/AGA/LGA · FGR and Doppler — definitions · Stages I–II · Stages III–IV

grupos.bajada: UA, MCA, CPR by percentiles; ductus venosus, tricuspid, aortic isthmus and umbilical vein.
grupos.html:
1UA, MCA and CPR by percentiles

  • FMF percentiles by GA (Ciobanu 2019).
  • UA PI >P95: increased placental resistance.
  • MCA PI <P5: cerebral vasodilation.
  • CPR <P5: cerebral redistribution; assess haemodynamic FGR. The CPR P5 is adjusted for GA.
  • CPR between P5 and P8: borderline; repeat in 1 week.

Based on: Ciobanu A et al. (FMF) UOG 2019;53:465-472 · Baschat AA, Gembruch U. UOG 2003

2Ductus venosus

  • Increased PI: venous dysfunction.
  • Absent a-wave: severe decompensation.
  • Reversed a-wave: severe decompensation; deliver.

Based on: Baschat AA. Obstet Gynecol 2011 · TRUFFLE Study Group. UOG 2020

3Tricuspid regurgitation

GradeManagement
AbsentPreserved fetal cardiac function.
MildClose surveillance; repeat Doppler in 48–72 h; assess DV, CPR and biophysical profile.
ModerateSignificant cardiac compromise; daily biophysical profile; consider delivery according to GA.
SevereSevere cardiac dysfunction: urgent delivery, referral to Fetal Medicine and neonatology.

Based on: Baschat AA 2011 · ISUOG Practice Guidelines FGR 2020

4Aortic isthmus

  • Normal PI: no advanced redistribution.
  • Raised PI: possible advanced cerebral redistribution; correlate with CPR and biophysical profile.
  • Reduced flow: onset of severe redistribution; intensive surveillance, repeat in 24–48 h.
  • Absent diastolic flow: severe haemodynamic compromise; imminent delivery depending on context.
  • Retrograde flow: maximal redistribution with left heart failure; urgent delivery.

Based on: Gratacós E, Torres X. Fetal Medicine Barcelona protocol 2023 · Arduini D, Rizzo G 1990

5Pulsatile umbilical vein

  • Mild pulsatility: intensive surveillance; repeat in 24 h; consider delivery according to GA.
  • Overt pulsatility: late fetal decompensation with venous congestion; urgent delivery coordinated with neonatology.

Based on: Baschat AA 2011 · TRUFFLE 2020

6Management with abnormal advanced Doppler

Coordinate with neonatology and refer to a tertiary centre. Timing of delivery depends on GA, biophysical profile and progression. For lung maturation and neuroprotection, see the cards Fetal lung maturation and Fetal neuroprotection with magnesium sulfate.

Based on: ISUOG Practice Guidelines FGR 2020 · ACOG Practice Bulletin 127 · ACOG 455

See also in Clinical History: FGR stages III–IV · Fetal biophysical profile

Reduced flow: onset of severe redistribution; intensive surveillance, repeat in 24–48 h. Absent diastolic flow: severe haemodynamic compromise; imminent delivery depending on context. Retrograde flow: maximal redistribution with left heart failure; urgent delivery.
fichas.fuentes: Based on: Gratacós E, Torres X. Fetal Medicine Barcelona protocol 2023 · Arduini D, Rizzo G 1990

fichas.texto: Mild pulsatility: intensive surveillance; repeat in 24 h; consider delivery according to GA. Overt pulsatility: late fetal decompensation with venous congestion; urgent delivery coordinated with neonatology.
fichas.fuentes: Based on: Baschat AA 2011 · TRUFFLE 2020

fichas.texto: Coordinate with neonatology and refer to a tertiary centre. Timing of delivery depends on GA, biophysical profile and progression. For lung maturation and neuroprotection, see the cards Fetal lung maturation and Fetal neuroprotection with magnesium sulfate.
fichas.fuentes: Based on: ISUOG Practice Guidelines FGR 2020 · ACOG Practice Bulletin 127 · ACOG 455

grupos.bajada: MCA peak systolic velocity and twin pregnancy follow-up.
grupos.html:
1Fetal anaemia — MCA PSV

MCA-PSVManagement
<1.29 MoMNo evidence of anaemia; follow-up per protocol.
1.29–1.49 MoMSurveillance; repeat in 1–2 weeks.
≥1.50 MoMModerate-severe anaemia: urgent cordocentesis and intrauterine transfusion.

Own algorithm CaVeSal® · Based on: Mari G et al. NEJM 2000;342:9-14

2Follow-up between transfusions

Serial MCA PSV allows timing of the second intrauterine transfusion.

Based on: Detti L et al. Am J Obstet Gynecol 2002;187:1048-1051

3Twin pregnancy — follow-up

  • Determine chorionicity and amnionicity in the 1st trimester.
  • Monochorionic: serial Doppler due to the risk of twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome.
  • Dichorionic: biometry every 4 weeks.
  • Refer to Fetal Medicine.

Based on: ISUOG Practice Guidelines — twin pregnancy · FMF · ACOG

4Selective FGR in monochorionic twins

TypeUmbilical artery Doppler
Type IUA Doppler of the smaller twin with positive diastolic flow.
Type IIPersistent absent or reversed diastolic flow.
Type IIIIntermittent absent or reversed diastolic flow.

Based on: Gratacós E et al. UOG 2007;30:28-34 · Torres X et al. Fetal Diagn Ther 2017

grupos.bajada: Fundal height percentiles and pre-pregnancy BMI with weight-gain targets.
grupos.html:
1Fundal height by percentiles

  • The Calculator compares fundal height with the 10th, 50th and 90th percentiles for GA. McDonald rule of thumb: FH (cm) ≈ GA ± 2 between 20 and 36 wk.
  • <P10: rule out FGR, oligohydramnios or discrepancy with amenorrhoea. Ultrasound with EFW and Doppler (UA, MCA, CPR).
  • >P90: rule out macrosomia, polyhydramnios, gestational diabetes, undiagnosed twins, fibroids or GA discrepancy.

Own algorithm CaVeSal® · Based on: Gomes AG. RBGO 2001 · CLAP-PAHO/WHO

2Weight gain by pre-pregnancy BMI

Pre-pregnancy BMITotal targetPer week in 2nd and 3rd trim.
Underweight (<18.5)12.5–18 kg~0.51 kg
Normal (18.5–24.9)11.5–16 kg~0.42 kg
Overweight (25–29.9)7–11.5 kg~0.28 kg
Obesity (≥30)5–9 kg~0.22 kg

Singleton pregnancy. In twins the targets are higher. The Calculator flags gain as excessive or insufficient when it deviates more than 1.5 kg from what is expected for the week.

Based on: IOM/NAS 2009 · ACOG

3Risks by pre-pregnancy BMI

  • Obesity: aspirin to prevent PE (see the Preeclampsia tab), early screening for gestational diabetes, BP surveillance and referral to nutrition.
  • Overweight: moderate risk of gestational diabetes, PE and macrosomia; GDM screening at 24–28 wk and BP surveillance.
  • Underweight: risk of FGR and preterm birth; calorie-protein supplementation and serial biometry.
  • Excessive gain: assess gestational diabetes and macrosomia. Insufficient: assess FGR, nausea or hyperemesis.

Based on: FIGO 2019 · NICE · ACOG · WHO

See also in Clinical History: Nutrition and weight gain · Physical examination by stage of pregnancy
Full sources for this tab: Calculator bibliography.

grupos.bajada: Probable Robson group, vaginal birth after caesarean and indications for planned caesarean.
grupos.html:
1Probable Robson group

During antenatal care the Calculator assigns a probable group with the available data. The definitive group is assigned at admission for birth (WHO). For example, a nulliparous woman at term with a cephalic fetus is placed in group 1 assuming spontaneous onset; if induction is planned she moves to 2a and if caesarean is planned, to 2b. If birth occurs before 37+0 wk, she moves to group 10.

The full classification and management by group are in the Emergencies guide: Robson classification and Management by group.

Own algorithm CaVeSal® · Based on: PAHO/WHO — Robson Classification implementation manual (2018) · FIGO 2025

2Vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC)

  • Candidate: one previous caesarean with a low transverse scar.
  • Favour success: previous vaginal birth and non-recurrent previous indication.
  • Assess carefully: potentially recurrent previous indication; previous uterine surgery according to myometrial extent.
  • Absolute contraindication: classical or inverted-T scar.
  • Two caesareans: counselling by a senior obstetrician. Three or more: planned caesarean.
  • The Calculator estimates the probability of success with the Grobman score.
  • Requirements: immediate surgical availability and informed consent; discuss the risk of uterine rupture (0.5–0.9 %). Misoprostol is contraindicated.

Based on: Grobman WA et al. (NICHD) 2007 · FIGO 2025 · ACOG

3Indications for planned caesarean

  • Transverse or oblique lie (absolute indication).
  • EFW ≥4,500 g (ACOG).
  • Classical or inverted-T uterine scar.
  • Breech presentation: caesarean recommended unless external cephalic version is successful (offer ECV from 36–37 wk if not contraindicated).
  • Without a medical indication, planned caesarean is not performed before 39 wk.
  • Short maternal stature with high EFW: suspected cephalopelvic disproportion.

Based on: ACOG · NICE · PAHO/WHO Robson 2018

4Gestational age at term

  • Preterm (<37 wk): assess lung maturation and coordinate with neonatology.
  • Term (37–41+6 wk).
  • Post-term (≥42 wk): increased risk; consider induction and biophysical monitoring.

Bishop score: see the Emergencies guide — Mode of delivery.

Based on: ACOG Practice Bulletin

See also in Clinical History: Placenta accreta spectrum · Fetal lung maturation
